findings.title: The paginator configuration is passed to get_result instead of the paginator constructor
findings.body: `Endpoint.paginate` forwards its extra keyword arguments to `paginator.get_result`, not to the paginator constructor. Therefore an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` calls `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result(..., enable_advanced_features=True)`, but that method does not accept this argument, resulting in an uncaught `TypeError` and a 500 response. Construct the paginator with this option (for example via a configured paginator class) or make the option part of the supported `get_result` contract.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry datetime ordering
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so `get_item_key` receives a `datetime` object. This implementation passes that object to `math.floor`/`math.ceil`, which only accept real numbers. `build_cursor` invokes this key function for any non-empty page, so the optimized audit-log path fails with a `TypeError` even if the constructor-option issue is corrected. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator's timestamp conversion behavior, or should inherit from DateTimePaginator.

findings.title: Negative-offset pagination uses unsupported QuerySet slicing
findings.body: The advanced branch passes a negative `start_offset` directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets reject slices with negative bounds (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`); they do not handle them as the comment claims. A permitted caller can supply a negative cursor offset, causing the audit-log request to fail with a 500 rather than providing reverse pagination. Implement reverse traversal using a valid cursor/range query, or reject negative offsets as a bad cursor.
